newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on talk of oil sale to China.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on talk of oil sale to China.

text.p: WCE canola ended up on talk of a sale of 20,000 tonnes of canola oil to China, traders said.

"The Chinese bought 20,000 tonnes of canola oil through Cargill and ADM. Normally they take 15,000 to 20,000 a month just with ADM so this Cargill talk has everyone talking," a trader said. ADM and Cargill were not immediately available for comment. Commission sell stops were triggered in July at $425 as traders realigned their positions ahead of Monday's USDA crop output report. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -2.75 Friday from -3.08 Thursday. About 500 July-Nov spread at $38. Volume was 4,980 lots, or 99,600 tonnes, with 605 hedge lots.
Japan bought 10-12,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
July canola rose $1.10 to $427.30, November up $3.20 at $390.60. July flax ended unchanged at $332.20 as commercials bought to cover old exports and sold November up $2 to $322.50.

May western barley rose $1 to $136.50, July up $0.10 to $137.20 on commission demand met by closing hedges but December lost $1 to $138.80 on commercial sales. May-July spread at $1.50. Volume was 525 lots. Oats did not trade.
July feed wheat lost $0.40 to $162.60 on closing hedges met by commission and local buying. Volume was 300 lots. UGG sold 10 May pea contracts down US$1 at US$214 to Cargill, a trader said.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
